extracted.intended_audience: installation commanders, contracting officers, commercial activities (A-76) study teams, and other government personnel conducting competitive sourcing studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and lessons learned for planning, conducting, evaluating, and managing OMB A-76 (competitive sourcing) studies on military installations, covering team structure, PWS development, acquisition strategy, risk management, milestones, and post-decision actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command support and leadership buy-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain and maintain support of the installation commander and key leadership; ensure key leadership 'buy into' the process and set the example for the study group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lesson learned emphasized obtaining and maintaining support of the installation commander; command support is critical to set the example and ensure study success. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Commercial Activities (CA) Team and functional subteams
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the CA Team into functional areas and subdivide into teams to examine the PWS, Management Plan, Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE) and QASP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: allows multiple tasks to be completed simultaneously while maintaining contact with the larger CA Team. Recommend an independent audit team to ensure baseline data consistency. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use full-time participants and bring in experienced personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff the CA Team with full-time participants where possible and consider bringing in retired civil service employees to provide functional expertise and assist workload data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed manning recommended full-time participants rather than part-time, and use of retired Civil Service employees for expertise and workload collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin team formation before Congressional notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate the A-76 team once it is known the process will occur, prior to Congressional notification, so the team can begin promptly when the formal clock starts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows the team to be ready to begin the study immediately after notification. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an open but controlled communication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish communication channels to pass information to and receive input from stakeholders without divulging information that could prejudice the MEO or offerors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: communication should not 'divulge information that could prejudice the MEO or offers or jeopardize the integrity of the A-76 process.' (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and track detailed milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Create detailed milestones for each commercial activity and track them in a system, updating promptly when schedules change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum recommended milestones: begin development of PWS and Management Plan; complete first draft of PWS; complete PWS; complete management study; complete in-house cost estimate; issue solicitation; begin source selection; notify major commands of initial decision; convene appeals board (if necessary); begin transition; fully implement contractor operations or MEO. (Ref. 20)

rubrics_metrics.name: Study entire function rather than piecemeal
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting an A-76 study, examine the entire function (e.g., Public Works) to create a properly staffed Most Efficient Organization (MEO) instead of fragmentary studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial studies risk perpetuating inefficiency because the MEO for the entire function is not created or staffed. (Ref. 20)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a Commercial Activity Executive Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an executive committee (chaired by the Installation Commander) including directors of functions studied, contracting officers, civilian personnel office, and major commands to monitor the study and make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also appoint a single individual to keep the study moving according to schedule. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish installation regulations and letters of instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish regulations and letters of instruction outlining responsibilities and duties of action officers and organizations participating in the A-76 study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps clarify roles and ensures consistent understanding of duties. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form an Acquisition Strategy Panel early
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a panel to address acquisition/business strategy early in the A-76 process, reviewing contract type, incentives, government property disposition, performance factors, maintenance responsibilities, and system interfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended issues for review: contract type; use of contract incentives; use and disposition of Government property; desired performance factors; maintenance and/or replacement by Government or contractor; required interfaces with automated info systems to ensure data collection for future contracts and higher HQ reports. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide contract type early and synchronize documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an early decision on contract type based on the nature of the work and obtain concurrence so PWS and contracting documents reflect the chosen contract type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids rework where contracting offices must change documents due to contract type changes; do not start certain contracting documents until contract type is decided. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop ground rules for unique labor sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine early how to treat unique labor sources (prisoners, volunteers, borrowed military personnel) in the PWS, MEO, and cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unique labor sources present challenges; develop policy addressing their inclusion or exclusion prior to study. (Ref. 20)

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect accurate, current workload data (fresh analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a fresh analysis of performance requirements and current internal processes to identify inputs, outputs, and internal controls rather than relying on prior studies as baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using previous performance requirement studies as the baseline; analyze current processes to prevent inaccuracies. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid adding tasks to skew cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not add tasks to surveys or PWS to 'stack the deck' in favor of the in‑house organization; such actions are often costlier and have little impact on contractor bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding tasks can make government estimates inaccurate and may lead to worse outcomes. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party validation of PWS and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a third party review and validate PWS requirements and operating procedures to ensure requirements are still performed and necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outside validation verifies accuracy and frequency of requirements; helps prevent inflated or outdated PWS items. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Allowable Quality Levels (AQLs) in solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that most service contracts cannot be perfect every time; allow establishment of AQLs with reasonable levels of effort for MEO or contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitation should allow AQLs so expectations are realistic and measurable. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct Performance Requirements Review before advancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a Performance Requirements Review prior to moving ahead with PWS and other portions of the study to ensure PWS accurately reflects actual work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid proceeding with an inaccurate PWS; mismatches have led to contractors bidding on inflated PWSs and MEOs winning at lower cost, causing protests and recompetition. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'Get Well' (do not add work to benefit MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assume the activity will gain additional manpower through the A-76 process by adding tasks; an MEO winning may lack personnel to perform added tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding work in hopes of 'getting well' can leave MEOs understaffed if they win, creating performance issues. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft PWS to state required outcomes, not methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the PWS to tell bidders what work is required rather than how to accomplish it; if specific approaches are necessary, place those in Section L and as evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prescribe contractor methods in PWS; use solicitation Section L and Source Selection Plan to require or evaluate specific approaches. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates cautiously and tailor PWSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use skeleton or prior PWSs as a starting point but tailor them to the installation's specific needs rather than copying old PWSs verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixed reactions: direct copying leads to inappropriate requirements; using templates as a jump-start and tailoring them helps meet specific needs and timelines. (Refs. 19, 20)

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve contracting personnel in PWS development
rubrics_metrics.description: Include contracting office personnel early in PWS development to incorporate necessary contract requirements and prevent later rework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting staff provide knowledge of contract clauses and requirements that must appear in the PWS. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain databases and contractor data access for PWS updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use database systems capable of updating the PWS when workload data changes; require contractor data access and include relevant contract clauses for data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government should have access to contractor-collected data about work performed and level of effort; include these requirements in PWS and contracts to enable updates. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accurate workload estimates to avoid change orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide accurate workload data so work requirements in the contract do not exceed actual workload figures, avoiding costly change orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess work in contract drives change orders and increases contract price. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform cost comparisons between MEO and bidders when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: When competition between the MEO and contractors is used, perform cost comparisons between the Most Efficient Organization and other bidders; if not performed, document reasons (e.g., direct conversion, incomplete studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey responses showed some commands used cost comparisons, others used direct conversion or were still finishing studies; document and justify the chosen approach. (Survey Q7)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Integrated Product/Process Teams and early contracting involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ Integrated Product/Process Teams (IPT) and involve contracting officers early in the study; include local union and keep government employees informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPTs are important for study conduct; contracting officer involvement early helps; keep stakeholders and unions engaged to manage transitions and employee concerns. (Multiple respondent lessons)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 'Best Value' source selection where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate employing a Best Value approach for competitive acquisitions rather than strictly lowest cost, to better capture performance and partnership aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One respondent recommended 'Best Value' and highlighted IPT importance in direct conversions as well. (Respondent #11)

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and plan for protests and Congressional input
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared for protests alleging costing errors or other issues and for letters to Congress; ensure costing processes are defensible and transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a protest alleging contractor-costing disadvantages was denied when costing was found correct; commands have also received letters to Congress likely from employees at risk. (Survey Q9)

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify significant risks and mitigation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically identify risk factors (manpower shortages, timeline pressures, protests, transition problems, security clearance delays, loss of in-house expertise, worker alienation, inability to capture workload data, local labor shortages, cost of studies, changing rules, mission impact, conflict of interest) and plan mitigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents listed many risk items: inadequate personnel to inspect/QA contractor functions; loss of in-house expertise over time; worker fear/negative reaction; inability to capture workload data; difficulty finding 'quality' contractors; minimum manpower levels; inability to meet published timelines; transition issues; security clearance delays (DIA averages 12-24 months); local labor shortages; cost of conducting studies; changing rules affecting ongoing studies; potential mission upheaval or loss of services; conflicts of interest via exposure to proprietary info. Develop mitigation: training, leadership involvement, realistic timelines, retain staff during transitions, fund studies, clarify guidance from higher HQ, and protect proprietary info. (Survey Q10 and multiple respondent lessons)
